follow_up_fixes: Issue 1: src/module_graph.rs check_selected_registry_modules no longer swallows repository_catalog::build failures with .ok(). In a writing lockfile mode a usage-table failure fails the command with the lazy-path error, and nothing is written (Bazel: BazelDepGraphFunction.getExtensionUsagesById :115-130 fails the command; no BazelDepGraphValue means no lockfile, :95-100).

Issue 2: src/bzlmod.rs records each repo-name usage as (how, location) (ModuleThreadContext.RepoNameUsage :105-113). Both profiles reserve bazel_tools (new BuiltinInjection::ReserveBazelTools for the explicit profile; AppendBazelTools also records the edge) and fail with Bazel's exact text (:115-125 + :383-401). The how values: by a bazel_dep / by a use_repo() call / by a repo rule / as the current module name / as the module's own repo name (ModuleFileGlobals :175-181, :317, :666-676, :867).

Found by follow-up row F2/local_use_repo: MODULE files of non-registry overrides (local_path, git) are now evaluated as @@<name>+//:MODULE.bazel (ModuleFileFunction.getModuleFile :752-777), so locations and diagnostics match Bazel. This was fixed after the follow-up run and verified native-only against the recorded Bazel text (both profiles equal). Also covered by tests/eager_resolution_mapping.rs non_registry_module_locations_use_the_canonical_module_file_label.

changes: repository_catalog: extension label failures use Bazel's text (BazelDepGraphFunction.getExtensionUsagesById :111-130): 'invalid label for module extension found at <first active use_extension lparen location>: no repo visible as '@X' here'. Syntax errors append the cause (ExternalDepsException.withCauseAndMessage :64-68). Isolated usages no longer skip unparsable labels silently.

module_graph: after every successful resolution (any lockfile mode, any registry kind) the eager usage table repository_catalog::usage_table is built. On failure the command fails with 'Error computing the main repository mapping: <message>'. Only Bazel's eager work is done here: label resolution with bazel_dep mappings, plus usage IDs and isolated prefixes for the lockfile. The native preparation catalog (repository_catalog::build) stays lazy. Making it eager would add native-only failures Bazel does not have, e.g. canonical-namespace validation of a raw use_repo_rule identity (module_graph test repo_rule_recording_uses_root_and_registry_dependency_contexts_without_mappings).
